title: [Chapitre] I. Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques) : notes manuscrites (05/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp.7-9): Grothendieck is axiomatizing 'forms of dimension 1', a combinatorial or synthetic substitute for 1-dimensional topological spaces such as graphs and curves. The data are:
- a set L of points;
- a set S of 'segments' I, each with a support Ĩ ⊂ L, an interior Ĩ° and a boundary ∂I ∈ P_2(L), the two-element subsets of L (endpoints);
- axioms F1-F5.
A point is regular if its order is ≥ 2, i.e. it lies in the interior of some segment. F5 says the order of every regular point is exactly 2. Its equivalent form F'5 says the interiors Ĩ° containing a regular point x form a filter base, a germ of 'neighbourhoods'. L_r and L_s denote the regular and singular loci.

This page has two remarks.

Remark 1: if S = ∅ (equivalently L_r = ∅, all points singular), the axioms hold trivially and the structure reduces to a bare set L, i.e. a discrete 0-dimensional form. Grothendieck then announces that in general one will have to include in the structure an intermediate datum: an equivalence relation on the singular locus L_s. Presumably this records identifications or 'branchings' at singular points, e.g. which ends meet at a vertex of a graph. The thread breaks off ('...').

Remark 2 (heredity): for an arbitrary subset L' ⊂ L, put S' = {I ∈ S | Ĩ ⊂ L'}. Restricting the two structure maps I ↦ Ĩ ∈ P(L') and I ↦ ∂I ∈ P_2(L') makes (L', S') again a model of a form of dimension 1 (F1-F5 hold). This answers, in greater generality, the question left open on p.7 for L' a union of segments.

Special case: L' = Ĩ for a single segment I. Then S' = S^I is the set of segments J with J̃ ⊂ Ĩ. Since a sub-segment of a segment is determined by its endpoints, S^I embeds into P_2(Ĩ). This prepares p.9: the case where L itself is a single segment, where a linear order on L is built from 'betweenness' [x, x_1].
errors: The condition in the special case is written 'Ĩ ⊂ I'; it should read J̃ ⊂ Ĩ (segments J contained in the support of I). This is a slip of notation.

Remark 2 is asserted without proof. The filter-base axiom F'5 restricts correctly, because any I with Ĩ ⊂ Ĩ' ⊂ L' lies in S'. Restriction can only lower the order of a point, so regular points of L may become singular in L'; this is harmless for F5. Whether F1-F4 (not visible here) survive needs checking, but it is plausible.

ideas.what: Degenerate case S=∅: a 1-dimensional form with no regular points is just a set; announced need for an extra equivalence relation on the singular locus
ideas.modern_name: 0-dimensional/discrete case; gluing data at vertices of a graph (vertex identification)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in graph theory and CW/cell-complex descriptions

ideas.what: Restriction of the structure to an arbitrary subset L' with segments contained in L' gives again a model (hereditary / induced substructure)
ideas.modern_name: induced substructure; universal (hereditary) axiom class; subspace of a 1-dimensional tame space

ideas.what: Segments contained in a given segment are determined by their endpoint pairs (S^I ↪ P_2(Ĩ)); preparation for a betweenness/linear-order description of a segment
ideas.modern_name: betweenness relations / ordered arcs (Hilbert, Huntington; arc characterizations by Whyburn, Ward)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pasch/Hilbert (betweenness axioms); Moore, Whyburn (characterizations of arcs)
ideas.where_published: Spirit related to 'topologie modérée' in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but not this axiomatics

missed.claim: Grothendieck foresees enriching the axiomatics of 1-dimensional forms with an equivalence relation on the singular locus L_s, as an 'intermediate' structure. This is a gluing datum not developed on this page.
missed.quote: On sera amené ... d'inclure dans la structure, en intermédiaire (dans le cas général) une relation d'équivalence sur L_s ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor. It is part of his program for a synthetic 'tame topology' of forms (1986), a project largely unexplored in the literature. Whether this datum is needed is only of interest to someone reconstructing that program.

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds routine structural remarks (trivial model, heredity under restriction, sub-segments determined by endpoints) inside an otherwise little-known 1986 axiomatization of 1-dimensional forms. The program as a whole is of historical interest, but this page has no notable result.
transcription_corrections: 'toutes les lignes sont singulières' is more likely 'tous les points sont singuliers' (L_r = ∅ means no regular point).
'se réduit à celle d'un ens. sur L' is probably 'se réduit à celle d'un ensemble L'.
'On sera amené tantôt d'inclure' is possibly 'On sera amené toutefois à inclure'.
In the special case, 'tels que Ĩ ⊂ I' should be read as 'segments J tels que J̃ ⊂ Ĩ' (superscript S^I added above the line).
